title: Provision verifier permits missing persistent rollback state and unsafe virgin defaults
description: Post-fix correctness review: ProvisionVerifier accepts rollback_state=None, exposes minimum_record_version=-1, and permits version0 installs despite spec requiring an explicit persistent minimum and saying default zero is insufficient. Distinguish authenticated virgin-state initialization from missing/corrupt storage, require an explicit persistence decision, fail closed on missing/corrupt state, and test first install/reboot/rollback.
notes: Fresh final robustness/security rereview remains NON-DRY: TimeAdmin.initialize_virgin_provision_state can be called repeatedly at any time and its persistence callback may be a no-op; every returned state remains accepted by the same admin. After a higher rollback floor exists, the same admin capability can mint a new virgin state and construct a fresh verifier at floor zero, bypassing the explicit persistent decision. Virgin bootstrap must be storage-authenticated, single-use/consumed, and distinguish first initialization from factory recovery; test sequential/concurrent remint and post-provision reuse.
